 ‘Newlyweds’ Recap: ‘Pilot’ 
 10/27/2026
 0 Comments
 Written by John Edward Betancourt  
 NEWLYWEDS -- "Pilot" Episode 101 -- Pictured: (l-r) Jamie Lee Curtis as Claudia, Tim Daly as James, Tea Leoni as Jeanie -- (Photo by: Nicole Weingart/NBC) 
 Caution: This article contains spoilers for the Series Premiere of ‘Newlyweds’.
​ 
Truly, there was a time in our world when whirlwind love affairs seemed to be the order of the day. Where two people would see one another across the room and immediately feel something within the depths of their soul. A connection for the ages that would lead to marriage and a lifetime of something we all seek: a true love that burns brightly no matter what the situation. But those days have passed. We are cautious now; we have more specific wants than just the eternal flame, and that has some people wondering if we’ve lost something by choosing a bit more logic in life over matters of the heart.
Yet there are others who are fine with playing it safe and doing it right and maintaining that flame through more modern means. Which leaves all of us wondering: is it possible to still see wild love affairs take place in the modern world? To see people just figure it out as they go? For that matter, what would it look like if we did see that in 2026? Well, a new series on NBC explores all of that in Newlyweds , and well, it poses the theory… it’s very possible to find such burning love in the 21st Century. But it would not be easy to maintain. Which the ‘Pilot’ explores by introducing us to James and Jeanie, a pair of folks who have had their fill of modern love.
Because they are not on the apps, and they are not really keen on how the current scene works. In fact, when we meet them, they’re attempting to avoid a blind date designed to fix them up. But once they cross paths and see one another… that draw of old arrives for them. Which leads to a whirlwind affair that the modern world threatens to derail. In part because James’ job requires him to travel, and that sends him to Europe for a few months, and that should cool their desire. But they cannot stop thinking about one another; they stay in touch, and Jeanie even goes so far as to sneak into his house to try and leave a gift, only to learn about his ex-wife, Claudia.
An eccentric and bold ex who is eager to just shake up James’ life because of the bitter nature of their marriage, and that too… should be the endgame for this affair. But the two of them persist; the two of them understand there is something special here and decide nothing will stop this. For they feel something few ever do: the burning love of legend, and they opt to do what isn’t the norm in this day and age and just get married and figure out the rest. A move that will absolutely test them. Since Jeanie’s two kids still live with her, James has Claudia and work to contend with, and that sets the stage for a fascinating and funny series.
For this is, at its core, a comedy, and this pilot does a great job of leaning into that as well. To speak to the absurdity of love and modern dating and to just make us chuckle. Through memorable moments and characters that shine and entertain, all through the lens of this unique story. One that reminds us that perhaps not all is lost in matters of love, that perhaps it still exists in that classical sense, and we’ve just forgotten how to find it and how to embrace it. Since it requires a little bit of openness and a lot of wild thinking to embrace its power and see where it takes us, and that’s what lies ahead for this series. A new journey, new challenges, and it will be fascinating to see where we go with this star-crossed couple in the weeks to come. Until next time.
